_what: How a workflow run's end is recorded in the database its row was read from (crates/workflow-component/src/main.rs `RUN_END`). Every pass that ends a run (completed, skipped or failed), whichever wake drove it (a chosen run, an answered step, a row change, a due row), asks this recorder once, unless the run names its own `on_end`. Its `with` paths read what the run knows at its end: run (the run's id, the wf_runs row its reader wrote at the start), status, workflow, why (null when it ended well) and database (the database of the run's own definition reader, `read_definition.input.database`). A run whose reader names no database records nothing: no store is named here. The statement upserts, so a run whose start row was never written still gets one. Why: Nov 22 2026, the end recorder was given in one wake's switch input only, so every run resumed by an answered step (319 keep-each-told-change-in-the-history runs from 9:58 PM CST Nov 21, the tennis chooser at 3:50 AM) ended with its row still saying started.

input.sql: INSERT INTO wf_runs (run_id, workflow, started_by, started_at, computer, status, failed, updated_at) VALUES ($1::text, $4::text, 'engine', now(), 'engine', $2::text, CASE WHEN $3::text IS NULL THEN '[]'::jsonb ELSE jsonb_build_object('why', $3::text, 'at', now()) END, now()) ON CONFLICT (run_id) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status, failed = CASE WHEN $3::text IS NULL THEN wf_runs.failed ELSE EXCLUDED.failed END, updated_at = now() WHERE wf_runs.status IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.status RETURNING run_id, status

reserve_steps_why: A run keeps two steps of its line for recording its end: the recorder's own run and the pass its answer starts. A pass that would hand out a step leaving fewer ends the run failed instead, and records that. Nov 22 2026, 4:44 AM CST: School's 27-step dry run spent all 40 steps of its line and record-the-end had none left, so its end was never recorded.
